title: Uncertainty of Vision Medical Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.30390v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate uncertainty estimation is essential for machine learning systems de- ployed in high-stakes domains such as medicine. Traditional approaches primarily rely on probability outputs from trained models (point predictions), which provide no formal guarantees on prediction coverage and often require additional calibra- tion techniques to improve reliability. In contrast, conformal prediction (region prediction) offers a principled alternative by generating prediction sets with finite- sample validity guarantees, ensuring that the ground truth is contained within the set at a specified confidence level. In this study, we explore the impact of pre-training approach, dataset scale and domain on both point and region-level uncertainty quantification, by studying domain-specific vision medical foundation models vs. general domain vision foundation models. translated_title: 视觉医学基础模型的不确定性
translated_abstract: 准确的不确定性估计对于部署在医学等高风险领域的机器学习系统至关重要。传统方法主要依赖于训练后模型的概率输出（点预测），这种方式无法对预测覆盖率提供正式保证，且通常需要额外的校准技术来提高可靠性。相比之下，保形预测（区域预测）提供了一种有原则的替代方案，通过生成具有有限样本有效性保证的预测集合，确保真实值在指定置信水平下包含于该集合之中。在本研究中，我们通过对比特定领域的视觉医学基础模型与通用领域视觉基础模型，探讨了预训练方法、数据集规模和领域对点级与区域级不确定性量化的影响。我们在多种基础模型上进行了全面评估，包括在视网膜、心脏等医学领域训练的基础模型。
tldr: 本研究通过对比医学领域专用视觉基础模型与通用视觉基础模型，系统评估了预训练方法、数据集规模和领域对点预测及保形预测不确定性量化性能的影响。
en_tdlr: This study comprehensively evaluates how pre-training approach, dataset scale, and domain affect point-level and region-level uncertainty quantification by comparing domain-specific medical vision foundation models with general-domain vision foundation models.
